summary: All 71 occurrences checked; repetitions of drowning reports remain distinct occurrence decisions but are not multiplied as independent examples.
Active causation includes manual strangling, smoke suffocation, hot-fat obstruction and water drowning. The last has repeated clear evidence for new sense2; the first three clarify inherited sense1.

Detransitive finite ḥniq/ḥnəqno and məḥnəq differ from expanded Part. Pass. ḥniqo/ḥniqe. Feminine ḥniqo can be finite or Part. Pass.; narrative sequence and copular environment decide, rather than surface -o alone.

A report of drowning can be negated, hypothetical or later disproved; the lexical meaning does not assert that the story participant actually died. Infectum-wa and Preterit can likewise describe prospective or counterfactual outcomes.
Legacy Prym–Socin references look like page/line citations and differ from supplied text/verse references. No citation is declared wrong solely because the numbering schemes differ.
The only proposed metaphorical new sense (financial strangling) is an extension of existing sense1, so no new idiom lookup was needed.
All 35 tokens checked independently; multiple same-verse repetitions at 1.44/1886 and 2.27/4561 remain separate decisions. Repetitions are not counted as independent supporting texts.
The reader’s D1 is the inherited shared sense 1, not a new label. Detransitive box prefixes are separated into canonical box names and detransitive=true in entry.json.

Round 1 already moves 65/177 out of Detransitive Preterit-wa and sets detransitive=false. Retain that correction without repeating it in this round’s JSON. Jan supplies genuine agentless ḥnəqwo in that now-empty Detransitive cell.

Finite ḥniqo in 1.59/2987 has feminine agreement with Fərdo; ḥniqo in 1.44/1886 and 1.59/2998 is a masculine state form with kəlle/mawfaqqe. Survival after 2985–2987 shows that a drowning report does not guarantee death.
kəḥniq explicitly supplies ko-Preterit at 2.2/251. Bare ḥniq nearby stays Preterit; English had drowned does not determine the box. Central ə in ḥnəqwo is preserved.

The chicken clause has lo and an omitted killer: it describes nonoccurrence of even a minimal killing, rather than a claim that a chicken actually died. No new slaughter sense is inferred from machine English.
Check the PrS legacy-to-text/verse concordance (43/33 versus PrS 18/38; 166/33 versus 60/102; 230/1 versus 78/82; 248/33 versus 85/19). Preserve existing references until mapped.
At 63/84, does Part. Pass. mean endangered/shipwrecked rather than completed drowning? The survivor context and copula suggest a state.
Check source translation typos at 45/23 ('er stickt') and 48/77 ('er trank'), and word order at 84/48; retain the edition wording until checked.
Confirm suffix segmentation at PrS 29/31 ḥniqulle and PrS 12/9 ḥənqatli without normalizing the printed forms.
Does the inherited Detransitive sense gloss intend both suffocation and strangling results? Existing smoke example makes its drowning-only wording too narrow.

Confirm ḥnəqwo as reduced Detransitive Preterit-wa across the pond reports and whether the default singular before noše/ḥəyewən (2.20/3819) and before 7 (2.29/4741) reflects ordinary agreement or a fixed saying.
At 1.59/2987 confirm finite feminine ḥniqo rather than Part. Pass.; at 1.44/1886 and 2998 confirm masculine result-state ḥniqo.
Is 2.29/4741 a fixed proverb with an allusive backstory? A bare quotation does not establish an idiom needing a glossary headword; supply the allusion before adding one.

Does the chicken expression at 3.56/1666 conventionally mean that not even a small thing is done for the community, or is the small-animal killing example literal? The Detransitive meaning is already supported by round 1.
Interest payments as a strangling agent are a financial metaphor already attested in the entry.
Detransitive drowning extends to ships sinking and goods included with drowned people; do not infer an additional lexical sense.

Jan supports round 1’s widened Detransitive choking/strangling gloss: animals can choke (1.50/2338), a cesspit suffocation proverb occurs (2.29/4741), and a chicken can be strangled (3.56/1666). An implied external killer does not require a new lexical sense.
